claim: INIT boots the centipede speed CENTIS to 2 — "FAST TO START WITH": the first wave runs fast, matching the port default; the slow/fast RESET below the 20,000 threshold only bites AFTER the CENTPC walk drives CENTIS to 3.

On each wave clear the register CENTIS is INCREMENTED ("FASTER") — the between-wave speed ramp. This INC is the engine of the whole progression: it is what eventually drives CENTIS to 3, unlocking the CENTPC length walk and the CONWAY / BOMBS wave gates.

Immediately after INC CENTIS the wave-clear code compares CENTIS with 3; only when it has just reached 3 (BCC skips below, BNE skips above) do the CONWAY / BOMBS wave-event gates below run. This is the same threshold the CENTPC walk uses to decide whether to DEC CENTIN.
When CENTIS has just reached 3 the wave-clear code loads the CURRENT CENTIN (the preserved wave-length register, read BEFORE the following CENTPC decrements it) to decide which wave event fires.
CENTIN is compared with 9: a match selects the CONWAY growth/death wave rather than a bombing wave or a plain wave.
On CENTIN == 9 the wave clear jumps to INICON, arming the CONWAY between-wave mushroom growth/death — so CONWAY is NOT started on every wave clear, only on the one whose CENTIN walked to 9.

BOMBS — the bomb-mode entry dispatcher — is JSR-ed every frame from the main creature loop; it is a no-op unless NOCENT is non-zero, so the per-frame call is the wiring seam that turns an armed bomb wave into dive-bombing critters.

source.verbatim: JSR BOMBS		;BOMB PLAYER WITH BEE, DRAGONFLY, ...
